package_info.package_manager: CDN (not a package registry, but distributed as a third-party JavaScript asset)
package_info.package_versions: All versions served after February 2024 takeover (exact versioning not applicable; dynamic CDN content)
package_info.why_malicious: The polyfill.js library, previously a trusted open source project, was taken over by a foreign actor in February 2024. The new operator injected malicious JavaScript into the assets served from cdn.polyfill.io, enabling arbitrary code execution in the browser context of any website including the script. This facilitated large-scale supply chain attacks, including user redirection to phishing or malware sites, credential theft via DOM access, and propagation of further malicious payloads through compromised client browsers.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, upon browser page load when the script is fetched and executed.
execution_context.file_location: Dynamically loaded via <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js?..."> in HTML or JavaScript files.
required_permissions: Network access (to fetch and send data to external domains)
DOM access (to read or manipulate page content and user input)
Full JavaScript execution in browser context (same privileges as first-party scripts)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the injected code executes in the browser context, performs unauthorized DOM access to read sensitive data or credentials, initiates network requests to attacker-controlled domains to exfiltrate this data, and may redirect the user to phishing or malware sites, resulting in user compromise and potential further malware propagation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The CDN, previously trusted, began serving JavaScript with undocumented and unauthorized behaviors, such as user redirection and data exfiltration to attacker-controlled domains. These are classic indicators of a supply chain attack leveraging a compromised third-party asset.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal polyfill libraries are expected to provide only compatibility shims for JavaScript features. They should never perform network requests to unknown domains, redirect users, or access sensitive data within the DOM.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate polyfill scripts only patch missing JavaScript features and do not interact with the network or user data beyond their intended purpose. They do not perform redirection, data exfiltration, or DOM manipulation unrelated to feature shimming.
key_indicators: Dynamic JavaScript served from a previously trusted CDN now under new, untrusted ownership
Injected code performing user redirection or data exfiltration to external domains
Behavioral changes in the script after domain ownership transfer in February 2024
Absence of version pinning or subresource integrity (SRI) in script inclusion
Polyfill script performing DOM manipulation or network requests unrelated to feature shimming

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the browser loads the page and fetches the external script.
execution_context.file_location: Static or dynamic script inclusion in HTML or JavaScript referencing cdn.polyfill.io or related malicious domains.
required_permissions: Full JavaScript execution in browser context

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the browser fetches and executes JavaScript from cdn.polyfill.io, which may contain malicious payloads that execute in the user's browser context, enabling arbitrary code execution, unauthorized DOM access, user redirection, or data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Including scripts from a compromised CDN allows attackers to inject arbitrary code into all websites that trust the CDN, enabling mass exploitation and supply chain compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Websites expect third-party CDNs to serve only the intended library code, not arbitrary or malicious payloads. Polyfill scripts should not introduce new behaviors or security risks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use is to load polyfills for browser compatibility, but not to execute untrusted or dynamically changing code that can perform actions outside of feature shimming.
key_indicators: Script inclusion from a domain known to be compromised or under new, untrusted ownership
No use of SRI or version pinning in script tags
Domain ownership and hosting changes to untrusted parties
References to suspicious or newly registered domains in script sources

attack_chain.action: Website includes a <script> tag referencing cdn.polyfill.io, trusting it to provide safe polyfill code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Browser fetches and executes JavaScript from the CDN.

attack_chain.action: Browser loads and executes the JavaScript payload, which now contains malicious code injected by the new CDN operator.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code runs in the user's browser context.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code performs actions such as redirecting users, exfiltrating sensitive data, or further propagating malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: User compromise, data theft, or further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: Runtime execution of JavaScript loaded from cdn.polyfill.io or related suspicious domains
Unexpected user redirection or network requests to attacker-controlled domains originating from polyfill scripts
Polyfill scripts performing actions beyond feature shimming, such as unauthorized DOM manipulation, credential access, or network exfiltration
file_indicators: References to polyfill[.]site, polyfill[.]com, bootcdn[.]net, bootcss[.]com, staticfile[.]net, staticfile[.]org, unionadjs[.]com, xhsbpza[.]com, union.macoms[.]la, newcrbpc[.]com in script tags or dynamic script loaders
Absence of Subresource Integrity (SRI) attributes for third-party scripts
Dynamic script loading from domains with recent ownership changes or flagged as suspicious
network_indicators: Outbound requests to cdn.polyfill.io, polyfill.io.bsclink.cn, and other listed suspicious domains
Unexpected network traffic to domains not previously associated with the application, especially after February 2024
Redirection chains leading to phishing or malware sites initiated by polyfill scripts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan all HTML, JavaScript, and template files for script inclusions referencing cdn.polyfill.io or related suspicious domains. Monitor runtime network activity in browsers for requests to these domains or for redirection events initiated by polyfill scripts. Use static analysis to flag any dynamic script loading from untrusted sources. Implement and enforce Subresource Integrity (SRI) and Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict and validate third-party script execution. Alert on any polyfill scripts performing actions beyond feature shimming, such as unauthorized DOM manipulation, user redirection, or network exfiltration. Correlate script inclusion with domain registration and ownership changes to identify supply chain risks.
